items.question: On 31 March 2026 a firm had stock ₹2,00,000, debtors ₹3,00,000, cash and bank ₹1,00,000, prepaid expenses ₹40,000 and current liabilities ₹2,00,000 (no bank overdraft). Its quick (acid-test) ratio is:
items.explanation: Quick assets are current assets less stock and prepaid expenses, so debtors plus cash and bank = ₹4,00,000. Divided by current liabilities ₹2,00,000, the ratio is 2 : 1.

why_not.A: That is the current ratio: all current assets ₹6,40,000 over ₹2,00,000.
why_not.B: Stock was removed but prepaid expenses were wrongly kept as a quick asset.
why_not.D: Only debtors ₹3,00,000 were counted; cash and bank were left out.

items.exam_tip: Quick assets = current assets minus stock and prepaid expenses. Prepaids cannot be turned into cash.
check_notes: Checker: Some textbooks include prepaid expenses in quick assets, which would give 2.2:1 (option B). The standard ICMAI/ICAI definition excludes them, so this is a possible but minor ambiguity.
Checker: Prepaid expenses act as a distractor. The question could say outright that quick assets exclude stock and prepaid expenses.

items.paper_name: Financial Management and Business Data Analytics
items.question: A firm has sales of ₹10,00,000, variable cost ₹6,00,000, fixed operating cost ₹2,00,000 and no debt or preference capital. What are its DOL and DFL?
items.explanation: Contribution = ₹4,00,000; EBIT = ₹2,00,000. DOL = Contribution/EBIT = 2. With no interest or preference dividend, EBIT equals EBT, so DFL = 1.

why_not.C: Divided sales less variable cost by something wrong: used 3,00,000 style base; contribution/EBIT is 2
why_not.D: Assumed DFL equals DOL; with no debt, DFL is 1, not 2
why_not.A: Swapped the two; fixed operating cost exists so DOL is not 1

items.exam_tip: DOL = Contribution ÷ EBIT. DFL = EBIT ÷ EBT. No interest means DFL = 1.
items.calculation:
contribution = 1000000 - 600000
ebit = contribution - 200000
answer = contribution / ebit
items.reviewer_note: Option B why_not text is awkward; consider rewording as "Used sales-based figure instead of contribution/EBIT". Answer is unaffected.

items.question: An open-ended scheme has 10,00,000 units outstanding. Market value of its investments is ₹12,50,00,000, cash balance is ₹50,00,000 and accrued expenses payable are ₹10,00,000. What is the NAV per unit?
items.explanation: NAV = (market value of investments + cash and other assets - liabilities) ÷ units outstanding. Net assets = 12,50,00,000 + 50,00,000 - 10,00,000 = ₹12,90,00,000, divided by 10,00,000 units.

why_not.D: Ignores accrued expenses payable; liabilities must be deducted.
why_not.B: Uses only investments and leaves out cash and liabilities.
why_not.C: Adds the liabilities instead of deducting them.

items.exam_tip: NAV per unit = (Assets - Liabilities) ÷ Units. Liabilities always reduce NAV.
items.calculation:
investments = 125000000
cash = 5000000
liab = 1000000
units = 1000000
answer = (investments + cash - liab) / units
